title: Introduction to the Ebrahim-Farrington Goodness-of-Fit Test
text: Goodness--fit testing crucial logistic regression assess whether fitted model adequately describes data. commonly used test Hosmer-Lemeshow test, several limitations: Limited power detecting certain types model misspecification Dependency grouping strategy can affect results Poor performance sparse data continuous covariates Ebrahim-Farrington test addresses limitations using modified Pearson chi-square statistic based Farrington’s (1996) theoretical framework, simplified practical implementation binary data.

code: set.seed(2026)  power_paired <- function(n, beta_quad = 0.15, n_sims = 200, G = 10) {   have_rs <- requireNamespace("ResourceSelection", quietly = TRUE)   rej <- c(EF = 0, HL = 0)   for (i in seq_len(n_sims)) {     x    <- runif(n, -2, 2)     y    <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(x + beta_quad * x^2))     fit  <- glm(y ~ x, family = binomial())      # misspecified: no quadratic term     p    <- fitted(fit)      # both tests see this same dataset     if (ef.gof(y, p, G = G)$p_value < 0.05) rej["EF"] <- rej["EF"] + 1     if (have_rs &&         ResourceSelection::hoslem.test(y, p, g = G)$p.value < 0.05) rej["HL"] <- rej["HL"] + 1   }   c(n = n, EF = unname(rej["EF"]) / n_sims,     HL = if (have_rs) unname(rej["HL"]) / n_sims else NA_real_) }  power_results <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, lapply(c(200, 500, 1000), power_paired))) print(power_results, row.names = FALSE) #>     n    EF    HL #>   200 0.070 0.065 #>   500 0.165 0.155 #>  1000 0.275 0.275

what: Pros and cons of partition-based tests
title: Goodness-of-fit and calibration tests for logistic regression
text: Pros - Intuitive — compare observed vs expected event counts within groups. - Work sparse data continuous covariates, classical Pearson deviance chi-square tests break (need replicated covariate patterns). - Widely used understood (Hosmer–Lemeshow de-facto standard). - Flexible — group fitted probability (HL, EF, Pigeon–Heyse, DEF) covariate space (Tsiatis, Xie) target different kinds misfit. Cons - result depends grouping choice — number groups G grouping rule. Hosmer–Lemeshow particular known give different answers different G across software. - Limited power departures — omnibus partition tests (HL) spread degrees freedom thinly; fitted-probability grouping can miss misfit cancels along predicted probability; covariate-clustering tests can miss smooth link departures. - chi-square reference asymptotic needs adequate group sizes. DEF built fix power cons without giving size control: keeps intuitive fitted-probability grouping directs test calibration-curve shapes, ensemble removes basis choice combining directions — tops table staying nominal size. Setup: covariate x ~ Uniform(-3, 3), models fitted glm(y ~ x); tests computed one call package’s run..gof(). dashed red line marks nominal 0.05 size.

code: # Function to simulate misspecified model simulate_power <- function(n, beta_quad = 0.1, n_sims = 100) {   rejections <- 0      for (i in 1:n_sims) {     x <- runif(n, -2, 2)     # True model has quadratic term     linpred_true <- 0 + x + beta_quad * x^2     prob_true <- plogis(linpred_true)     y <- rbinom(n, 1, prob_true)          # Fit misspecified linear model     model_mis <- glm(y ~ x, family = binomial())     pred_probs <- fitted(model_mis)          # Test goodness of fit     test_result <- ef.gof(y, pred_probs, G = 10)          if (test_result$p_value < 0.05) {       rejections <- rejections + 1     }   }      return(rejections / n_sims) }  # Calculate power for different sample sizes power_results <- data.frame(   n = c(100, 200, 500, 1000),   power = sapply(c(100, 200, 500, 1000), simulate_power) ) print(power_results)

code: # Example 1: Binary data with automatic grouping (Ebrahim-Farrington test) set.seed(123) n <- 500 x <- rnorm(n) linpred <- 0.5 + 1.2 * x prob <- 1 / (1 + exp(-linpred)) y <- rbinom(n, 1, prob)  # Fit logistic regression model <- glm(y ~ x, family = binomial()) predicted_probs <- fitted(model)  # Perform Ebrahim-Farrington test with 10 groups result <- ef.gof(y, predicted_probs, G = 10) print(result) #>                 Test Test_Statistic   p_value #> 1 Ebrahim-Farrington      -1.250567 0.9344997  # Example 2: Compare with different number of groups result_4 <- ef.gof(y, predicted_probs, G = 4) result_20 <- ef.gof(y, predicted_probs, G = 20)  # Example 3: Grouped data (original Farrington test) set.seed(456) n_groups <- 50 m_trials <- sample(5:20, n_groups, replace = TRUE) x_grouped <- rnorm(n_groups) linpred_grouped <- -0.5 + 1.0 * x_grouped prob_grouped <- 1 / (1 + exp(-linpred_grouped)) y_grouped <- rbinom(n_groups, m_trials, prob_grouped)  # Fit model for grouped data data_grouped <- data.frame(successes = y_grouped, trials = m_trials, x = x_grouped) model_grouped <- glm(cbind(successes, trials - successes) ~ x,                       data = data_grouped, family = binomial()) predicted_probs_grouped <- fitted(model_grouped)  # Original Farrington test. G = NULL is required: left at its default of 10 the # call takes the automatic-grouping branch instead, which ignores 'model' and 'm' # and refers binomial counts to the binary statistic. result_grouped <- ef.gof(y_grouped, predicted_probs_grouped,                          model = model_grouped, m = m_trials,                          G = NULL) print(result_grouped) #>                  Test Test_Statistic   p_value #> 1 Farrington-Original     -0.2010413 0.5796669

title: ebrahim.gof 2.0.0
text: def.gof() - Directed Ebrahim-Farrington (DEF) goodness--fit test. Projects grouped standardized residuals onto smooth calibration-shape basis ("poly2", "poly3", "stukel") calibrates statistic weighted sum chi-square_1 variables (Satterthwaite default; Imhof via suggested CompQuadForm). basis = "ensemble" shortcut def.ensemble.gof(). def.ensemble.gof() - combines three DEF bases (optionally omnibus EF, extra p-values) one decision via Cauchy combination test (default), minp fisher offered comparison. ef.gof(), def.gof(), def.ensemble.gof() now accept either fitted glm (y, predicted_probs) input. def.gof, supplying design matrix X (y/predicted_probs form) gives exact calibration; without conservative chi-square reference used warning issued.

title: ebrahim.gof 2.0.0
text: ef.gof() now defaults chi-square reference (method = "chisq"): grouped statistic referred chi-square_{G-2} distribution. Use method = "normal" reproduce previous (standardized-normal) p-value. run..gof() - one-shot runner returns tidy data.frame, one row per test. Pass fitted glm whole battery, (y, predicted_probs) prediction-tests. One failing test never aborts run. build bundles Pearson, Deviance, Osius-Rojek, Copas-RSS, Hosmer-Lemeshow (deciles equal-width), Pigeon-Heyse, EF, three DEF bases, Stukel, covariate-space tests Tsiatis, Xie, Pulkstenis-Robinson, two Cauchy-combination ensemble rows. Osius-Rojek, Copas-RSS, Pigeon-Heyse, Tsiatis, Pulkstenis-Robinson verified match original implementations ~1e-15 (Xie’s statistic also matches). run..gof() tests verified reproduce implementations used original thesis simulation. particular Osius-Rojek Stukel now follow LogisticDx::gof.glm (Stukel via statmod::glm.scoretest; statmod added Suggests), matching numerically; Copas-RSS matches rms’s gof residual; HL matches ResourceSelection::hoslem.test; HL-equalwidth, Pigeon-Heyse, Tsiatis, Xie, Pulkstenis-Robinson match source scripts. second EF row, EF-normal, reports omnibus EF test normal reference used thesis simulation (EF row uses chi-square default). opt-slow (include_slow = TRUE) tests: GAM-based HL-GAM, PR-GAM, Xie-GAM (Xie et al. 2021; need mgcv; HL-GAM PR-GAM match source gam_gof_tests exactly, Xie-GAM uses fixed clustering seed), Stute-Zhu (cumulative-residual parametric-bootstrap test; sequential, set reps via control = list("Stute-Zhu" = list(B = ...)); statistic matches source exactly). Lai-Liu-HL (Lai & Liu 2018, standardized-power procedure Hosmer-Lemeshow test). p-value: resamples target size, fits model, estimates HL rejection rate (“standardized power”), returns randomized accept/reject decision. standardized power reported statistic decision Note (set n0/k via control). Verified match source lai_liu_test exactly. Two opt-slow tests: eHL (e-value Hosmer-Lemeshow test Henzi et al. 2024; base-R reimplementation, attribution, marius-cp/eHL code, matching ~1e-11; reported p = min(1, 1/e)), BAGofT (binary-adaptive GOF test, wrapping BAGofT package; set nsim via control = list(BAGofT = list(nsim = ...))). opt-slow test, le-Cessie (le Cessie-van Houwelingen 1995, general multivariate smoothed-residual test), runs include_slow = TRUE. O(n2)-O(n3). Adapted attribution USGS smwrStats package (public domain); verified match exactly. Xie test uses corrected degrees freedom G - k/2 - 1 k number predictors. (Earlier thesis runs used df = G - 0.5, artifact coef() returning NULL predicted-probability list; statistic , p-value differs.) Added Information-Matrix test (White 1982 / Orme 1988), closed-form IM test; verified match thesis IMtest_fast exactly.
